source.extract: A horizon is a boundary in spacetime satisfying prescribed conditions. There are several types of horizons that play a role in Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity: Absolute horizon, a boundary in spacetime in general relativity inside of which events cannot affect an external observer Event horizon, a boundary in spacetime beyond which events cannot affect the observer, thus referring to a black hole's boundary and the boundary of an expanding universe Apparent horizon, a surface defined in general relativity Cauchy horizon, a surface found in the study of Cauchy problems Cosmological horizon, a limit of observability Killing horizon, a null surface on which there is a Killing vector field Particle horizon, the maximum distance from which particles can have travelled to an observer in the age of the universe
